You take what you have and put it where it's needed, and it goes out by measure. Nobody had to haul it out of you. What you hand over lands, and the people around you stand up steadier because of it, though they may not say so.

This runs well when help comes back as light — something you already finished reaches its own end and you get to stand in that for an hour. The bend now is that you keep checking the scale instead of letting the flow move: is this too much, will they expect it again. Put the scale down for one turn.
1.sheetLine: You give by measure. You just keep checking the scale.

2.tense: You will be holding everything before anyone has asked you to.
2.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it
2.place: becoming what you are
2.ask: When the fix comes to you today, say not yet once — no apology attached.
2.core:
The future is the room you're furnishing. Before anyone reaches for it, the thing is already in your hands — the bill covered, the problem half-solved, the worry taken. You call it being reliable. It's a grip that lands ahead of the moment it belongs to.

This holds well when it carries what's actually there without crushing it. The bend is that you're lifting weight that hasn't arrived, and it doesn't get set down, so it doesn't land anywhere. Strength spent early leaves nothing when the real need shows up, and the real need tends to show up on someone else's schedule. The next ask can wait for the ask.
2.sheetLine: You're lifting things nobody has handed you yet.

3.tense: You stopped offering your strength back when offering it went where you didn't want.
3.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it
3.place: becoming what you are
3.ask: Pick one person and one thing you can hand over this week, then hand it over and stop.
3.core:
You've gone quiet with what you have. Your hands are full and the need around you is real, and you let it pass without reaching. There's a door you brought your strength to once, and you don't go near it now.

What this looks like running clean: it holds without forcing, and it starts where you've already finished something, not where you're trying harder. You don't need more endurance for this. The strength is still in your hands; what went quiet is the offer. One small yes, said out loud where someone can see it, is enough to start it moving again.
3.sheetLine: You have something to give and you've stopped giving it.

4.tense: You are already shaping what happens next around you, and you're calling it just being helpful.
4.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it
4.place: becoming what you are
4.ask: Name the part of this you're actually doing — out loud, once, to whoever is closest.
4.core:
Look at how you spent the last few days. Money moved, favors landed, someone got back on their feet — a lot of it had your hands on it. It isn't luck and the room just happens to be okay. You were the one making it, and it won't sit right until you say so.

This runs clean when the shine comes from something that reached its own finish, not from management. Right now you're doing the turning and keeping your hands off the claim. Say out loud that the turn was yours, and what you give stops being a current that passes through and becomes something you chose to hand over.
4.sheetLine: You're doing the shaping. You just haven't claimed it.

1.tense: You are carrying what you carry and laying it down where the need is, with the pen.
1.verb: moving your strength outward to whoever is holding more than they can carry
1.place: standing inside the whole and seeing it at once
1.ask: For a month, keep one standing arrangement exactly as it is, and each week name one thing you are not adding to that day.
1.core:
You put strength where it is needed and you know how much is enough. That takes sense, not force, and from where you stand you can see who is carrying too much before anyone has to tell you. The pattern usually arrives whole, all at once, and you move.

It holds while you keep stopping. Even a body trained for a long time reaches a point where straining breaks it rather than holds it, and you can feel that line. What you have built needs your pull now, not more of your pushing, and the cultivating that earned this is already done. Make the adding a choice instead of a reflex, and let what is already working be enough for a while. The arrangement you keep unguarded is the one that shows you whether it is.
1.sheetLine: You share your strength by measure now, and you know the measure.

2.tense: You are already holding the next thing that has not been handed to you, ahead of anyone asking.
2.verb: moving your strength outward to whoever is holding more than they can carry
2.place: standing inside the whole and seeing it at once
2.ask: Name one load you are not obligated to hold, and drop the first task you took on for it today, before anyone agrees.
2.core:
You are already braced under what has not been handed to you. Before it is asked for, before it is yours, you have sized the weight, taken your position, and made the offer. And you can see the whole pattern from here, so every gap looks like a place your strength is needed, and you get there before the need does.

The size is not the issue; the timing is. Holding can hold without forcing, and yours is forcing. The fairness you can feel has not been checked against anyone. Test one gap before you lift. Ask whether the person on the other side is standing already. Say no to one thing today and watch what happens without stepping back in. That is not coldness. Carrying what no one needed carried is how the thing that did need you goes uncovered.
2.sheetLine: You lift before the ask arrives, and you call it being needed.

3.tense: You saw what was needed and stayed at the door where the asking used to go wrong, and you are still standing there.
3.verb: moving your strength outward to whoever is holding more than they can carry
3.place: standing inside the whole and seeing it at once
3.ask: Pick one arrangement you already see and set one definite condition on it this week — the day, the amount, the end. Then hold that one.
3.core:
You can see the whole thing. You can point to the exact place the weight sits and who is bending under it, right now, while you talk. What is missing is the movement between seeing and doing. Your strength stays home while the picture stays clear in front of you.

Being able to see it is not the problem, and it was not a failure. The step is small: make one arrangement you already see definite, with a condition on it. Not a bigger heart, not a wider door. An arrangement with an end sends a stream back through the watching. When something you set is finished, you can lay it down instead of gripping it, and what you notice has somewhere to go again.
3.sheetLine: You see where the strength is needed and you are not moving it.

4.tense: You are holding people up right now and calling it being able to help when someone asks.
4.verb: moving your strength outward to whoever is holding more than they can carry
4.place: standing inside the whole and seeing it at once
4.ask: Pick one thing you are already carrying for someone this week and say out loud why you kept doing it this way.
4.core:
You are already the one, in this. People come to you and something clears. The strength is moving outward and it is doing its work, and you describe it as a convenience, the capable one, no big deal. Where you are standing, the whole pattern is visible, so you keep agreeing to be the fixed point for it without ever saying that you chose it.

So the strength that helps most is the one you admit to. Pick one thing you are already carrying for someone and tell them what you are going by, why this, why this long. Not a confession, one sentence at a time, in your own plain words. Once you name who decided, the same effort stops feeling like something that happens to you and starts feeling like yours, and it will not be the last one.
4.sheetLine: You are already the one holding this. You are calling it nothing.

1.tense: You are handing resources to people who need them, and the giving is clean.
1.verb: putting strength in the hands of whoever needs it next
1.place: the threshold where finished things are released into what comes next
1.ask: Name out loud the one thing all your helping is for. Then keep it where you can see it for a week without adding anything to it.
1.core:
You are the one who makes sure things reach where they're needed. What you carry goes out and lands, and you know the shape of what you're handing over — the weight is measured, not thrown at people. People take what you offer because it fits.

What's true underneath is that you're past the middle of something. A thing you've been building is close to done, and handing it off is how it finishes. What comes next grows out of what you've already carried. If it feels like you're between things right now, that isn't a gap — it's the open door your own work just made.
1.sheetLine: You give by measure, and what you've carried is nearly through.

2.tense: You are standing in a future where nobody needed you, and you are trying to earn your way back from it.
2.verb: putting strength in the hands of whoever needs it next
2.place: the threshold where finished things are released into what comes next
2.ask: Let one offered help go unanswered today. Say thank you once and do nothing else with it — no follow-up, no repayment. Let it land.
2.core:
You are giving ahead of the need. Before anyone asks, you have already decided what they should have, and deciding has stopped being about them. At the far end of that is a room where it all worked and you're standing in it with nothing left to hand over. So you keep producing more, harder, to make sure the end stays away.

That's the cost: what you share has become a debt you are trying to pay off. The fairness you're looking for doesn't need a ledger. It's the plain sense of what's genuinely owed, and you already have it most days. Stop, and let someone turn an offer down without you replacing it.
2.sheetLine: You are giving ahead of the need and calling it support.

3.tense: You stopped offering what you had and the moment you stopped is still behind you.
3.verb: putting strength in the hands of whoever needs it next
3.place: the threshold where finished things are released into what comes next
3.ask: Pick one thing you've been holding for someone else and hand it back today, to hold or drop as they choose. Say why you're returning it.
3.core:
There was a point where sharing stopped and it hasn't started again. You have strength that could go out — resources, steadiness, a way of showing up that others used to lean on — and it stays in the box. You call it not knowing what people need, but that isn't what went missing. The offering is.

The strength itself is fine. It's the place it flows from that's worn thin. Trying to push generosity from a dry well just hollows you further. What fills it is committing to one real thing and staying with it when friction shows up — not more helping, but engagement that tests what you're actually for.
3.sheetLine: Your strength is still here. The offering is what stopped.

4.tense: You are already holding things steady for people and you are calling it nothing much.
4.verb: putting strength in the hands of whoever needs it next
4.place: the threshold where finished things are released into what comes next
4.ask: Write down one thing you do that holds someone steady, in your own hand. Then say 'that's mine' about it once, out loud, before you put the paper away.
4.core:
You have been the one people lean on, and you would not put it that way. Your being steady is real — friends feel it, family counts on it, it shapes how a room goes when you're in it — yet you describe it as if the situation were doing the work. You are the one keeping it up.

Seeing it plainly isn't vanity. It's the ground you'd need to notice why your helping works and what it might be for next. You keep the lights on for other people. Your light comes from what you genuinely built, not from carrying more.
4.sheetLine: You are already holding things steady. Claim it as yours.
